_: Bonitz's own errors: preserved in work/reconciled, corrected in the revised edition. See README.md.

entries.authority: τέχνη is barytone — the nominative accents the penult — and a noun's accent is persistent, staying where the nominative puts it unless a long ultima forces it forward. The accusative singular is therefore τέχνην. LSJ s.v. τέχνη.
entries.note: The acute stands plainly over the η of -νήν, well clear of the χ, and the line's other accents (μαθήσεις, πρὸς, τὰς) are set normally. LlamaParse read τέχνην, i.e. it silently corrected the print. Preserved as printed per the diplomatic rule. ⚠ The authority field first cited Smyth §163 for this, which is wrong and was caught in adversarial review (Grok, 2026-08-08): §163 limits how far back the accent may stand, and says nothing against a first-declension oxytone — τιμή, τιμήν are perfectly legal. The objection to τεχνήν is not that the ultima cannot be accented in the declension, but that THIS noun does not accent it. The classification was right; the citation was not.

entries.authority: Genitive plural of κακόν requires omega; the ou-ligature spells ου, which gives no word here. Sense: εἴ τις αἰτίαν ἔχει κακῶν τοὺς γονέας.
entries.note: The printed glyph is IDENTICAL to the ligature in `τȣ̀ς` on the same line and unlike the ω of `ἀνωλέθρον` on 017-R — so the compositor set the ligature where an omega belongs. John ruled `κακῶν (omega)` in July against the 300 dpi 1955 reprint; at 400 dpi the ink does not support it. Preserved as printed per the diplomatic rule; banked for the revised edition.

entries.authority: The article τῇ is dative singular, so the noun must be ἀκριβείᾳ with the iota subscript. Smyth §216.
entries.note: The accent placement our reader has is right — the acute is on the -εί- of ἀκριβεία, not on the first ι as LlamaParse read it — but the final α carries no subscript in the ink, while the τῇ two words earlier plainly does. Bonitz's own omission; preserved.

entries.authority: ἁλίζω 'to salt', from ἅλς, takes the rough breathing. The entry is about salted bread (ἠλισμένοι, opp ἄναλοι).
entries.note: The ink has the SMOOTH — identical in shape to `ἄρτοι` beside it, and unlike the rough on `ὑπὸ` at l.42. Bonitz prints it smooth; preserved. family.py had 'corrected' it to rough by propagation from the ruled headword ἁλιεύς, and that was reverted.

Same line carries `ὑπὸ` with a plain rough (reversed comma, opening left) against this word's smooth (comma, opening right) — the two glyphs are distinct at 400 dpi. John ruled the same lemma smooth at l.15 in July. Occurrences at ll.38, 40, 41, 43, 44 are the same word and the same ruling.
